statements.text: And we see companies that are leading in this space.
statements.context: Remarks delivered at a hearing titled 'Trustworthy AI: Managing the Risks of Artificial Intelligence.'

statements.text: We need to prioritize STEM education to ensure that we have the fundamental knowledge base for students across the country to get into this field because we are going to need more coders and ethicists in this field who actually can assist with our leadership. The other thing I think would be important to note, too, is that we also need to make sure that we have talent in this country and retain talent and still attract talent. And one of the things that we found out through our AI Commission is that we, you know are going to lose the talent race if we don't deal with our immigration issues in this country as well and make sure that we can retain talent after we've educated them here in the United States, make sure that we can keep our talent to ensure that we have people who know how to make ethical AI work.
statements.context: Remarks delivered at a hearing or event titled 'Trustworthy AI: Managing the Risks of Artificial Intelligence.'

statements.text: I think, given the state of the technology, we believe it's premature to get into prescriptive regulation. We support voluntary frameworks like we see at NIST. [...] we'd like to see a national standard put in place. But at the same time, we want to make sure that the process at NIST can work itself out first before we start making any kind of determinations on regulation.
statements.context: Remarks delivered at a policy event titled "Trustworthy AI: Managing the Risks of Artificial Intelligence."

statements.text: Well, I think it's interesting to know, during one of our hearings, we actually had one of the cochairs of the National AI Advisory Committee come testify, Miriam Vogel. [...] And it's important that we have real firm guidance in place. [...] there is some teeth there.
statements.context: House hearing titled 'Trustworthy AI: Managing the Risks of Artificial Intelligence', with Rep. Crenshaw discussing standards and compliance.

statements.text: we need more education out there about the need to build in ethical AI into standards for companies and how they operate. [...] I've talked to some companies that are actually developing their own ethical frameworks and have full-time ethicists who are being brought on.
statements.context: Remarks delivered at a hearing or event titled 'Trustworthy AI: Managing the Risks of Artificial Intelligence.'

statements.text: I agree that C-suite needs to be involved. [...] But at the same time, I think with the work we're seeing at agencies like NIST are getting us in the right direction toward where we want to be.
statements.context: Remarks by Rep. Dan Crenshaw at a hearing titled 'Trustworthy AI: Managing the Risks of Artificial Intelligence.'

statements.text: At any moment they could demand that all of TikTok's data be used to design an AI algorithm with the sole purpose of promoting Chinese interests and destroying our society from within.
statements.context: Congressional hearing on safeguarding American data privacy and protecting children from online harms, focused on TikTok's relationship with the Chinese government.

statements.text: Congressman, as a member of the military and the Securities and Exchange Commission, I think we need to look holistically at AI across the board and not look at it just necessarily in the isolated world of financial background or the military side. [...] but also learn where we need to put holistic protections in place and how we can sort of learn from it and adopt appropriately.
statements.context: Verbatim remarks during a congressional oversight hearing on the Securities and Exchange Commission.
